title: SSDL-ILT: Efficient ILT utilizing a self-supervised deep learning model
problem: Inverse lithography technology (ILT) for mask optimization is hindered by time-intensive physical simulation; pixel-level mask optimization requires expensive iterative refinement.
motivation: Advanced chip manufacturing requires efficient ILT but simulation cost limits practical deployment; self-supervised learning can eliminate expensive label data requirements.
method: This approach uses a deep learning model trained without needing labeled examples—instead, a specially designed loss function guides the training by scoring how well the predicted masks work. The model directly outputs the final chip mask patterns and automatically generates tiny supporting features called SRAFs (sub-resolution assist features) that help ensure the design is manufacturable, with adjustable control over manufacturing difficulty. This eliminates the time-consuming physical simulations and iterative refinement previously required.
key_novelty: A deep learning model trained without labeled data that automatically generates optimized chip masks and sub-resolution assist features (SRAFs) to avoid iterative physical simulations.
contributions: Self-supervised deep learning approach to ILT
Novel loss function for unsupervised mask optimization
Automatic SRAF generation with complexity control
Up to 12,000x speedup vs SOTA models
Good generalization to geometrically-different patterns via few-shot learning
primary_theme: self-supervised learning for inverse lithography technology
